b:
that the loading bar going from 50 to 60% is
god. The first scream of “YEAH” from Usher’s mouth
reaching between my little stream of internet,
Lil John trickling from LimeWire’s belly to my ears
is holy. I am anointed by Deacon Piration
who offers me, no tithing required, an all
-inclusive trip to salvation. Ain’t he alright—
Lyfe Jennings singing a sinner’s prayer? The hard
learnings of S.E.X. through the family desktop
on a school night? I loaded all these holy
hymns to my iPod Nano, took it to school
to make the Mary Magdalenes say Damn,
you got all the jams! LimeWire gave me
a smile that stretched over a thousand seas
till I realized: I left Back to Black downloading
on accident—damn; the desktop prematurely
went on to glory. I could give a testimony
of my Job-like punishment or tell you joy comes
like a thief in the night (like stealing
my daddy’s password). Let’s skip Bible study,
let every serving of a false god
freeze like the screen of my Windows XP.
Let’s stay up all night to watch that green
-and-yellow lime go, & go, & go—
Listen to KB Brookins on this episode of the Poetry Magazine Podcast.
